I implemented `convert()` in `src/billing/currency.py`. It multiplies the integer cents by the Decimal rate and rounds toward negative infinity with `ROUND_FLOOR`. That follows the Treasury rounding decision, so a conversion never credits more than the rate allows. It takes and returns integer minor units, with no floats.

I ran a quick check: 1005 × 0.5 gives 502, 100 × 1.009 gives 100, and −1005 × 0.5 gives −503. Because it floors, negative amounts such as refunds round away from zero. If Treasury meant something different for those, that needs a decision. I did not add a test file.

An edit hook flagged the "Invoice PDF rendering" memory (01a0fc48-c3eb) as possibly affected. I did not check it, and `convert()` has no obvious link to PDF rendering, so it is probably a false positive.
